https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/baltic-.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:04 Baltic States will develop joint electricity system reserve capacity Translated by Karolis Broga Source: ELTA Saulės ir vėjo elektrinės PHOTO: APChanel | Shutterstock Follow Delfi on Google The energy ministers of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have agreed to develop joint reserve capacity for the Baltic energy system, which would allow electricity supply to be restored more quickly for residents and businesses in the event of various threats or damage to critical infrastructure. On Wednesday, Lithuania’s Minister of Energy Lukas Savickas, together with Latvian and Estonian counterparts, signed a joint declaration on the development of the reserve capacity for the Baltic energy system. „Geopolitical tensions and increasingly frequent natural disasters caused by climate change pose growing challenges for energy infrastructure. Joint reserves and an agreement to coordinate actions during emergencies will help ensure a more reliable energy supply for residents, while shared solutions will allow to strengthen the security of energy infrastructure more effectively and at a lower cost,“ says Savickas. Under the agreement, electricity transmission system operators of the Baltic States will jointly assess the emergency power grid equipment, which is needed to ensure the fastest possible restoration of electricity supply in all three Baltic countries in the event of various threats or disruptions. The emergency equipment may include transformers, transmission poles, generators and other reserve resources. After completing the joint assessment, it is planned to submit a joint application for European Union funding in order acquire and maintain reserve capacity at the level of the Baltic region.
